AGENDA TITLE:        Notice of Exemption for Vegetation Maintenance Within the Truckee
Tahoe Airport Airfield

MEETING DATE:           Oct 21, 2026
PREPARED BY:            Vince Wawrzynski, Operations Director


RECOMMENDED ACTION: Truckee Tahoe Airport District Board of Directors approve Notice of
Exemption (NOE) for vegetation management on the airfield.
Background:        The Tahoe Truckee Airport District (TTAD) seeks to conduct vegetation
maintenance within the airfield for the purposes of airport safety. This NOE is a means of
complying with California Environmental Quality Act prescriptions. The total acreage covered by
this NOE is approximately 915 acres (Attachment A-1). Vegetation maintenance may be
necessary and/or mandated by law for the safety of planes entering and exiting the airfield, and
may include but is not limited to herbicide application, hand cutting, chipping (tracked or tow-
behind), piling, burning, and/or mastication of woody fuels and live vegetation. The airfield has
been highly disturbed for many years for the construction of runways and associated grading, etc.
These processes are covered under an existing Mitigated Negative Declaration that is unrelated
to vegetation management (SCH No. 2015122021).
Fiscal Impact: Minor. The District will pay both Nevada and Placer Counties processing fees, less
than $200.00.

earned his ACE Safety Management Systems certification on February 13, 2026, within his first six
months of employment.

accelerated achievement and demonstrated professional development.

AGENDA TITLE:         Contract approval for Situational Awareness Display RFP
MEETING DATE:         October 13, 2026
PREPARED BY:          Mike Cooke, IT Manager


RECOMMENDED ACTION: Approve a 5-year contract to Airport Systems Information Exchange,
“ASiX,” the selected vendor in a competitive bid process per TTAD’s PI 303 to provide a situational
awareness display for KTRK ATC and staff. This continues the Airport District’s commitment to
enhance safety by providing real-time airspace and movement area operations monitoring for
staff and ATC.
BACKGROUND:
The existing contract for this service expired earlier this year and staff requested a 6-month
extension, which ended Sept 30th, to review existing service needs and research new features
and options. This also ensured that implementation of any changes could be accomplished under
off-season and quieter traffic volumes. Situational awareness tools for staff and ATC (opened in
2018) have been in use by the Airport District since 2011. While only available for use in an
advisory capacity, KTRK’s ACT and staff may use the display to track aircraft in the region and
monitor equipped ground targets such as snow removal equipment and operations vehicles.
SAI displays, as they are more commonly called in larger facilities, are being embraced and
encouraged by the FAA for their cost-effective and often more cutting-edge, modern features.
As an industry leader in GA technology, TTAD has provided ATC with situational awareness tools
since opening the airport-sponsored tower in 2018.
Vendors were requested to submit proposals for a situational awareness display to be used in an
advisory capacity that can enhance overall safety in the region. The selection was based on value,
overall RFP criteria requirements, prior projects, functionality, and many additional enhanced
features.
DISCUSSION: Staff recommend contract approval to the selected RFP bidder, ASiX for a 5-year
term consisting of 3 regular and 2 option years.

                                                                                        1|Page
                                   OCTOBER 21, 2026

FISCAL IMPACT:

Five-year contract value at $148,096. First year savings over previous agreement of $12,000
with around $50k savings over full term when compared to nearest competitive bid.
SAMPLE MOTION(S): I move to (approve, deny) the 5-year contract with ASiX to provide KTRK
ATC and staff with a real-time situational awareness display tool for use by staff and only in an
advisory capacity at ATC to enhance overall safety for the Truckee Tahoe Airport District at large.

                  TRUCKEE TAHOE AIRPORT DISTRICT
                  BOARD OF DIRECTORS STAFF REPORT



AGENDA TITLE: Noise Operations Monitoring System (NOMS) – RFP Decision

MEETING DATE: October 21, 2026

PREPARED BY: Jeff Menasco, Director of Aviation
             Larry Finney, Safety, Security, Community Engagement Manager


RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Board approve or disapprove a generic scope of work for a Request For Proposal (RFP) for
implementation of a Noise Operations Monitoring System (NOMS).

DISCUSSION:
The Board has previously discussed the potential benefits and costs of implementing a Noise
Operations Monitoring System (NOMS) at Truckee Tahoe Airport. NOMS could support three
District objectives:

   1. Community Engagement: Provide additional information to help staff respond to aircraft
      noise complaints and communicate noise impacts to the community.

   2. Noise Abatement Evaluation: Evaluate the effectiveness of existing noise abatement
      procedures and identify opportunities for improvement.

   3. Long-Term Trend Analysis: Monitor changes in aircraft noise exposure over time and
      support data-informed decisions.

Staff contacted four vendors to obtain Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimates for available
noise monitoring technologies, system capabilities, implementation requirements, and associated
costs.
Because vendors were not provided with a standardized scope of work, estimates vary in
configuration and services and should not be considered as directly comparable proposals.



                                       October 21, 2026
                                                                                        1 | Page

Vendor: configuration                        Startup estimate    Annual estimate
V1a: purchase 7 physical NMTs**              $247K               $102K
V1b: lease 7 physical NMTs                   $72K                $147K
V1c: virtual-only                            $42K                $97K
V2: base software, no hardware               Not provided        From $35K
V3: physical monitor per site                $23-33K             $1,500–$2,000 per NMT
V4a: virtual grid reporting; 20+ locations   Not specified       $30K
V4b: optional permanent physical NMT         ~$10K per unit      Maintenance extra
**Noise Monitoring Terminal
The following alternatives reflect a combination of preliminary vendor information and staff
estimates.

Option A – Virtual NOMS / Light Hybrid (Staff Preferred)
Estimated annual cost: $50,000–$100,000

A software-based approach that models aircraft noise using flight tracking data, aircraft
characteristics, and other inputs without relying on permanent physical noise monitors. This
approach would provide modeled geographic noise exposure, historical trends, and information to
support community engagement and evaluation of noise abatement procedures. Based on price
points and potential to re-calibrate TTAD owned NOMS sensors, there might be an opportunity to
leverage some portable devices under option-A, though this is not guaranteed or the focus of this
option.
    • Lowest anticipated cost and implementation complexity.
    • Broad geographic coverage without physical equipment installation; potentially some
        sensors.
    • Provides modeled rather than directly measured noise levels; potentially some sensors.

Option B – Hybrid NOMS
Estimated annual cost: $50,000–$150,000

Combines virtual noise modeling with a limited number of physical noise monitors, potentially
including temporary or mobile devices. This approach would allow the District to compare
modeled noise estimates with actual measurements at selected locations.
    • Balances geographic coverage, physical measurements, and cost.
    • Provides flexibility to investigate specific locations or community concerns.
    • Requires additional equipment, maintenance, management, and potential land leasing.



                                         October 21, 2026
                                                                                          2 | Page

Option C – Comprehensive NOMS
Estimated annual cost: $150,000–$400,000

A comprehensive system combining virtual noise modeling with a network of permanent physical
noise monitors throughout the surrounding community. This approach would provide continuous
measured noise data at selected locations, detailed trend analysis, and additional tools for
community engagement.
    • Most extensive physical noise monitoring capability.
    • Provides continuous measurements at selected locations.
    • Highest anticipated acquisition, operating, potential ground leasing, and maintenance
       costs.
Three-Year Cost Comparison
The following table illustrates the estimated cost of each NOMS alternative over a three-year
period. Estimates are based on preliminary vendor information and staff planning assumptions.

NOMS Alternative                             Annual Cost          Three-Year Operating Cost
Option A – Virtual NOMS             (Staff
                                             $50K–$100K           $150K–$300K
Preferred)
Option B – Hybrid NOMS                       $50K–$150K           $150K–$450K
Option C – Comprehensive NOMS                $150K–$400K          $450K–$1.2M

Note: Three-year estimates assume constant annual costs and exclude one-time startup, equipment
acquisition, and installation expenses. Actual costs would be determined through the RFP process.
The comparison illustrates the potential long-term financial differences between the alternatives.
While more extensive physical monitoring can provide additional measured noise data, it also
introduces higher equipment, maintenance, and operational costs.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends Option A – Virtual NOMS as the preferred approach for developing an RFP. A
virtual system offers the potential to support the District's three primary objectives—community
engagement, noise abatement evaluation, and long-term trend analysis—at a substantially lower
cost and with less implementation complexity than a permanent physical monitoring network. It
should be noted that there is a “potential” to leverage TTAD owned noise sensors, however they
would need to be calibrated and may no longer be usable. Based on RFP, there might be low-cost
option to deploy portable sensors for a limited amount of time.

Although virtual systems model, rather than directly measuring noise levels, staff believe this
approach provides an appropriate starting point to evaluate the value of a NOMS before
committing to more costly physical monitoring infrastructure.

Staff recommend proceeding with an RFP to establish system capabilities, limitations, and actual
costs. Staff would evaluate proposals and return to the Board with a recommendation for

AGENDA TITLE:         Amendment of the Conflict-of-Interest Code Pursuant to the
                      Political Reform Act of 1974
MEETING DATE:         October 21, 2026
PREPARED BY:          Lauren Tapia, HR Manager/District Clerk


RECOMMENDED ACTION: It is recommended that the Board of Directors: (1) adopt Resolution
2026-05 adopting the District’s amended Conflict of Interest Code pursuant to the Political
Reform Act of 1974; and (2) approve Policy Instruction 204 – Conflict of Interest Policy 2026,
which incorporates and codifies the same amendments.
BACKGROUND: The Political Reform Act of 1974, Government Code Section 81000 et seq. (the
“Act”), requires all public agencies to adopt and maintain a Conflict-of-Interest Code. The Act
further requires that agencies regularly review their codes on a biennial basis and update them
as necessary when directed by the code-reviewing body or when change is necessitated by
changed circumstances (Sections 87306 and 87306.5). The Fair Political Practices Commission
(“FPPC”) is the District’s code-reviewing body and directed the District to complete its 2026
biennial review.
On September 7, 2026, the District filed its 2026 Multi-County Agency Biennial Notice with the
FPPC, reporting that staff’s review of the code had been completed and that an amendment was
necessary.
DISCUSSION: During the biennial review, staff worked with the BBK’s Public Policy and Ethics
Compliance specialist to evaluate all positions created, retitled, or reorganized since the Code
was last amended on October 28, 2020. The review determined that the following amendments
to the Code are necessary:
New positions to be designated:

   •   Deputy General Manager – Categories 1, 2
   •   Deputy Director of Airport Operations and Maintenance – Categories 2, 3, 5, 6

                                                                                       1|Page
                                  OCTOBER 21, 2026

•   Facilities Maintenance Manager – Category 5
Revision of title:

   •   Airport Safety & Security Manager retitled to Airport Safety, Security, and Community
       Engagement Manager (remains Category 5)
Positions to be deleted:

   •   Aviation & Community Services Manager – Noise/Annoyance
   •   Aviation & Community Services Manager – Property
   •   Aviation & Community Services Manager – Public Relations
   •   Aviation & Community Services Program Coordinator (Safety)
   •   Operations & Maintenance Assistant Supervisor
Other revisions:

   •   Minor language revisions to the disclosure categories in Part “B” of the Code to better
       reflect current District programs and duties
   •   Updated Form 700 filing requirements for §87200 filers to reflect newly enacted CA SB
       852, which requires public officials who manage public investments to file their Statement
       of Economic Interests (Form 700) directly with the FPPC rather than through the local
       filing officer
A notice of intention to amend the Code was posted on September 6, 2026, establishing a 45-day
comment period for District employees and the public in compliance with Title 2, California Code
of Regulations, Section 18750, which ran through October 21, 2026. A legislative (redlined)
version of the proposed amended Code, showing all changes described above, is attached for the
Board’s review. Policy Instruction 204 – Conflict of Interest Policy 2026, also attached,
incorporates the Code as it would read if the proposed amendments are adopted.
FISCAL IMPACT: None.

AGENDA TITLE: Adoption of Revised Policy Instruction (PI) 507 — Non-Profit Use
              of Airport Non-Aviation Lease Space and Post-Occupancy Rent
              Discount Policy by Asset Class

MEETING DATE: October 21, 2026

PREPARED BY: Jeff Menasco, Director of Aviation


RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Adopt revised Policy Instruction (PI) 507, Non-Profit Use of Airport Non-Aviation Lease Space —
Community Benefit Selection Criteria, Lease Process, and Post-Occupancy Rent Discount Policy by
Asset Class.

DISCUSSION:
PI 507 currently establishes criteria and procedures for selecting community benefit tenants for
vacant non-aeronautical space but does not expressly address rent discount treatment following
occupancy. Historically, certain warehouse tenants have received rent discounts of approximately
sixty percent (60%). The proposed revision establishes a framework for future Board consideration
of rent discounts by District asset class, while preserving Board discretion to approve, modify, or
discontinue discounts.

The revised PI 507 retains and clarifies existing tenant-selection criteria and lease procedures
(Sections 1–3), and adds a post-occupancy rent discount framework (Section 4) addressing five
categories:

   ● Warehouse Building — historical discounts of approximately sixty percent (60%) serve as
     nonbinding guidance, not a ceiling, standard rate, or entitlement. The Board may approve
     a lesser or greater discount, or no discount.
   ● Non-Aeronautical Open Land / Shipping Container Sites (approximately 12 sites) — CAM-
     only treatment, with no base rent, is identified as guidance for qualifying community
     benefit tenants, subject to Board discretion.


                                     October 21, 2026                                  1 | Page

● Aeronautical (Airside) Land and Facilities — no rent discounts on property designated for
     aeronautical use under the proposed policy, consistent with the District’s federal
     compliance objectives.
   ● Civil Air Patrol, Phoenix Hangar (Standing Exception) — continued no-rent occupancy is
     expressly authorized by the policy without recurring Board reauthorization; future
     modification, termination, or expansion requires Board action.
Section 5 requires Board review and reauthorization of discounts at each lease renewal; no
discount carries forward automatically. The Board also retains authority to review, modify, or
revoke a discount between renewals, consistent with the applicable lease agreement.

FISCAL IMPACT:
Discounts approved for non-aeronautical warehouse space and open land/container sites may
reduce lease revenue relative to market rates. The proposed policy provides that such reductions
are offset using the District’s non-airport ad valorem property tax revenue, rather than
aeronautical or other airport revenue. Adoption alone does not establish a new discount or amend
an existing lease; any fiscal effect will depend on future Board actions and applicable lease terms.
The proposed policy prohibits discounts on aeronautical land and facilities. Federal compliance
considerations should be reviewed with District counsel, including FAA Grant Assurance 24 (Fee
and Rental Structure), Grant Assurance 25 (Airport Revenues), and Grant Assurance 22 (Economic
Nondiscrimination).

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS:
None required beyond standard Board agenda posting requirements.

Item 4. Truckee High School Paid Internship Program
Two interns have been funded by the Youth Jobs Core program in the State of California via
Connecting Point, we expect them to begin in November 2026. This program expanded to East
Nevada County and offering Truckee High School students who meet the requirements to work
a 3–6-month, 20 hour a week, paid internship (paid by Connecting Point) with new participating
entities in the area (Truckee Library, Truckee Tahoe Helping Hands, Town of Truckee, and Truckee
Airport). This will be a new program we will be offering to help develop general aviation skill sets
of interns for future potential employment with the District - as opportunities become available.




Item 5. Warehouse Fire Sprinklers Installation
Installation of the Warehouse fire sprinklers starts on 10/20/26 and will likely continue into early
January. The contractor is starting with the west side Non-Profit tenants first, which is expected
to take about 5 to 6 weeks or through the late part of November. The east side warehouse
installation will be from late November to early January.


Item 6. Flight Awareness Display
We are transitioning from “Airboss” to “ASiX” flight awareness displays. This is primarily used by
our ATC tower controllers for aircraft awareness but also used in dispatch. This new situational
awareness information system has multiple upgrades to include: an Expanded Surveillance
Coverage Area, Target and Clutter Management Tools, Operation Mapping, replay capability,
Map in Map functions for monitoring critical areas, pavement area management to highlight
closed and NOTAM’d segments, and dedicated human support during tower hours.
